findings.text: The pipeGroups Map uses inputStream as the key, but when multiple output streams (e.g., stdout and stderr) both pipe from the same input stream type, they will incorrectly share the same array. For example, if both stdout and stderr have transform streams, the second one will overwrite or merge incorrectly with the first, causing data to be piped to the wrong subprocess.stdio fd.

When direction is 'input', the code sets inputStream to subprocess.stdio[fdNumber] and outputStream to the user stream, then uses inputStream (subprocess.stdio) as the Map key. This means multiple input streams targeting the same subprocess stdio will be grouped together incorrectly, causing the wrong merge behavior in the final piping loop.

The outputFiles Set tracks paths as strings, but path can be a URL object (fileUrl type). When the same file URL is passed twice, path.toString() may produce different string representations (e.g., with or without trailing slashes), causing appendFileSync to be used incorrectly instead of writeFileSync, or vice versa.

When direction is 'input' and a duplicate is found, the function returns undefined, but the caller in handle.js line 427-428 expects a stream value. This causes the input stream to not be properly set, breaking input piping for duplicated input file descriptors.

When an error is thrown during getFinalFileDescriptor, cleanupCustomStreams is called on the partially built fileDescriptors array, but the streams in the fileDescriptor that caused the error (which was not yet pushed) are not cleaned up, causing a resource leak.
